papers.title: Microbial Methanogenesis on Mars: A Life Detection Target for an MLE-Type Mission and Future Human Exploration
papers.abstract: Methane (CH4) is one of the most enigmatic and potentially consequential trace gases detected on Mars, having demonstrated apparent seasonality, localized plumes, or, depending on who you ask, never conclusively detected at all. While the Martian methane mystery remains unsolved, it has sparked a vibrant area of astrobiology research exploring whether microbial methanogenesis -- one of the simplest and most ancient metabolic pathways -- could plausibly proceed under various extreme physicochemical conditions characteristic of the Martian shallow subsurface. The emerging consensus is a cautious but compelling "possibly". These findings elevate methanogenesis as both a top priority candidate biosignature for extant life detection and a justification for urgently advancing in situ instrumentation capable of definitively detecting CH4 and constraining its origin, biotic or otherwise
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Methane is a simple gas, made of one carbon atom surrounded by four hydrogen atoms. On Mars it has become a stubborn puzzle. On Earth, living microbes produce most of our methane, although some geological processes can make it too. Spacecraft and instruments have reported what look like seasonal rises and falls, and localized plumes, of methane on Mars. Other researchers argue it has never been conclusively detected at all. If methane is really there, and if life made it, that would be one of the biggest discoveries in the history of science.

**What They Did**
This paper surveys a lively area of research rather than reporting a single new measurement. Scientists in this field ask whether microbial methanogenesis could work in the shallow Martian underground. Methanogenesis is a way for microbes to make a living by producing methane, and it is one of the simplest and most ancient forms of metabolism known. Think of it as asking whether a very hardy tenant could survive in a harsh, remote basement. The studies examine a range of extreme physical and chemical conditions found in that environment.

**Key Findings**
The emerging consensus is a cautious but encouraging "possibly." Microbes that make methane could plausibly operate under the extreme conditions of the Martian shallow subsurface. Because of this, the authors rank methanogenesis as a top-priority candidate biosignature, meaning a chemical sign that could point to life that exists on Mars today. The abstract is clear that this does not prove life is there. The origin of Martian methane, and even how reliably it has been detected, remains an open question.

**Looking Forward**
The authors argue that these results justify urgently developing better instruments that can work directly on Mars. Those instruments would need to detect methane with confidence and help show whether it comes from biology or from non-living processes. The paper frames this as a target for a Mars Life Explorer-type mission, a mission concept focused on searching for life, and for future human exploration of Mars.

papers.title_tr: Mars'ta Mikrobiyal Metanojenez: MLE Tipi Bir Görev ve Gelecekteki İnsanlı Keşif İçin Bir Yaşam Arama Hedefi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Metan, bir karbon atomunun dört hidrojen atomuyla çevrelenmesinden oluşan basit bir gazdır. Mars'ta ise inatçı bir bilmeceye dönüşmüştür. Dünya'da metanın büyük kısmını canlı mikroplar üretir, ancak bazı jeolojik süreçler de metan oluşturabilir. Uzay araçları ve aletler Mars'ta metanın mevsimsel olarak arttığını ve azaldığını, ayrıca yerel bulutlar (kümeler) halinde görüldüğünü bildirdi. Başka araştırmacılar ise metanın hiçbir zaman kesin olarak saptanmadığını savunuyor. Metan gerçekten oradaysa ve onu yaşam ürettiyse, bu bilim tarihinin en büyük keşiflerinden biri olurdu.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Bu makale, tek bir yeni ölçümü bildirmek yerine canlı bir araştırma alanını gözden geçiriyor. Bu alandaki bilim insanları, mikrobiyal metanojenezin Mars'ın yüzeye yakın yeraltında işleyip işleyemeyeceğini soruyor. Metanojenez, mikropların metan üreterek enerji elde etmesini sağlayan bir yöntemdir ve bilinen en basit ve en eski metabolizma biçimlerinden biridir. Bunu, çok dayanıklı bir kiracının sert ve uzak bir bodrumda hayatta kalıp kalamayacağını sormaya benzetebiliriz. İncelenen çalışmalar, bu ortamda bulunan çeşitli uç fiziksel ve kimyasal koşulları ele alıyor.

**Ana Bulgular**
Ortaya çıkan görüş birliği temkinli ama umut verici bir "belki"dir. Metan üreten mikroplar, Mars'ın yüzeye yakın yeraltındaki aşırı koşullarda makul biçimde faaliyet gösterebilir. Bu nedenle yazarlar metanojenezi, bugün Mars'ta var olan yaşama işaret edebilecek kimyasal bir iz, yani öncelikli bir aday biyoimza olarak değerlendiriyor. Özetin açıkça belirttiği gibi bu, orada yaşam olduğunu kanıtlamaz. Mars metanının kökeni ve hatta ne kadar güvenilir biçimde saptandığı hâlâ açık bir sorudur.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlar, bu sonuçların Mars üzerinde doğrudan çalışabilen daha iyi aletlerin acilen geliştirilmesini haklı çıkardığını savunuyor. Bu aletlerin metanı güvenle saptaması ve onun biyolojik mi yoksa cansız süreçlerden mi kaynaklandığını belirlemeye yardımcı olması gerekir. Makale bunu, yaşam aramaya odaklanan bir görev kavramı olan Mars Yaşam Kaşifi (Mars Life Explorer) türü bir görev ve Mars'ın gelecekteki insanlı keşfi için bir hedef olarak sunuyor.

papers.title: Granulation in Color: The Chromatic Stellar Flicker of LTT-9779 and WASP-121
papers.abstract: Granulation is a persistent feature of stars with outer convective layers and is the photospheric signature of near-surface convective energy transport. In disk-integrated observations, it produces stochastic brightness variations that contribute substantially to stellar variability on timescales of minutes to hours. High-precision, observations with JWST provide an opportunity to study the chromatic signatures of stellar granulation. This work aims to measure the amplitude and characteristic timescale of granulation-induced variability for solar-type stars and to investigate whether the granulation signal shows significant chromatic variation in the near-infrared. We accessed publicly available JWST/NIRISS SOSS time-series observations of LTT-9779 (G7V) and WASP-121 (F6V) and de-trended the light curves by fitting the transits, eclipses, and planetary phase curves. We computed power spectra from the de-trended light curves and fit them with a Harvey granulation profile. We first analyzed the broadband light curves to measure and fix the granulation timescale and then repeated the power-spectrum analysis in individual wavelength channels to measure the chromatic dependence of the granulation amplitude. For LTT-9779, we measure a broadband granulation amplitude of σ=53.8⁺⁴.¹₋₄.₀ppm at a timescale of τ=4.8⁺¹.⁵₋₁.₃min. For WASP-121, we measure σ=59.3±4.3ppm and τ=6.3⁺².¹₋₁.₈min. We also measure peak oscillation frequencies of ν=3382⁺¹⁶⁶₋₁₉₁μHz and 1649⁺⁵⁵₋₆₉μHz in the bandpass-integrated power spectra of LTT-9779 and WASP-121, respectively. In the spectroscopic fits, we find σ decreases with wavelength. Our results demonstrate a new observational window on short-timescale stellar variability and provides a way to characterize chromatic stellar noise in transit light curves.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Stars are not perfectly steady lamps. Like a pot of simmering soup, the outer layers of Sun-like stars bubble constantly, with hot gas rising and cooler gas sinking. This churning creates a patchwork of bright and dark cells on the stellar surface, called granulation. We cannot see individual cells on distant stars, but together they make a star's brightness flicker randomly over minutes to hours. For astronomers studying planets, this flicker is a source of noise that can muddy measurements of starlight. Knowing how strong it is, and whether it looks different in different colors of light, helps us read planetary signals more cleanly.

**What They Did**
The team reused publicly available observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), taken with an instrument called NIRISS SOSS that splits starlight into a rainbow of near-infrared colors. They studied two stars: LTT-9779, a Sun-like star, and WASP-121, a somewhat hotter one. First they subtracted the signals of the orbiting planets: dips as planets pass in front, dips as they hide behind the star, and gradual brightness changes around the orbit. What remained was the star's own flicker. They then split that flicker into fast and slow rhythms, much as you might separate bass from treble in music, and fitted a standard mathematical model to it. They did this for all the light combined, and then color by color.

**Key Findings**
For LTT-9779, the flicker has an amplitude of about 54 parts per million (roughly 0.005% of the star's brightness) and a characteristic timescale of about 4.8 minutes. For WASP-121, the amplitude is about 59 parts per million and the timescale about 6.3 minutes. The power spectra also show peaks at about 3382 and 1649 microhertz for the two stars, respectively. When the light was split into individual colors, the flicker's strength decreased toward longer wavelengths.

**Looking Forward**
The authors say this opens a new observational window on short-timescale stellar variability. It also offers a way to characterize color-dependent stellar noise in the light curves used to study transiting planets.

papers.title_tr: Renkli Granülasyon: LTT-9779 ve WASP-121 Yıldızlarının Kromatik Yıldız Titreşimi
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Yıldızlar mükemmel derecede sabit birer lamba değildir. Kaynayan bir çorba tenceresi gibi, Güneş benzeri yıldızların dış katmanları durmadan kabarcıklanır: sıcak gaz yükselir, daha soğuk gaz aşağı iner. Bu çalkantı, yıldız yüzeyinde granülasyon denen parlak ve karanlık hücrelerden oluşan bir desen yaratır. Uzaktaki yıldızlarda tek tek hücreleri göremeyiz, ancak hep birlikte yıldızın parlaklığının dakikalar ile saatler arasında rastgele titremesine yol açarlar. Gezegenleri inceleyen gökbilimciler için bu titreşim, yıldız ışığı ölçümlerini bulandırabilen bir gürültü kaynağıdır. Titreşimin ne kadar güçlü olduğunu ve farklı renklerdeki ışıkta farklı görünüp görünmediğini bilmek, gezegen sinyallerini daha temiz okumamıza yardımcı olur.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, James Webb Uzay Teleskobu'nun (JWST) herkese açık gözlemlerini yeniden kullandı. Veriler, yıldız ışığını yakın kızılötesi renklerin bir gökkuşağına ayıran NIRISS SOSS cihazıyla alınmıştı. İki yıldız incelendi: Güneş benzeri LTT-9779 ve biraz daha sıcak olan WASP-121. Önce yörüngedeki gezegenlerin sinyalleri çıkarıldı: gezegenler yıldızın önünden geçerken oluşan düşüşler, arkasına saklanırken oluşan düşüşler ve yörünge boyunca yavaş parlaklık değişimleri. Geriye yıldızın kendi titreşimi kaldı. Bu titreşim, müzikte bas ile tizin ayrılması gibi hızlı ve yavaş ritimlere bölündü ve standart bir matematiksel modelle (Harvey profili) uyduruldu. Bu işlem önce tüm ışık birleştirilerek, sonra renk renk tekrarlandı.

**Ana Bulgular**
LTT-9779 için titreşimin genliği yaklaşık milyonda 54 (yıldız parlaklığının kabaca %0,005'i), karakteristik zaman ölçeği ise yaklaşık 4,8 dakikadır. WASP-121 için genlik milyonda yaklaşık 59, zaman ölçeği yaklaşık 6,3 dakikadır. Güç tayflarında ayrıca iki yıldız için sırasıyla yaklaşık 3382 ve 1649 mikrohertz'de tepeler görülmektedir. Işık tek tek renklere ayrıldığında, titreşimin şiddeti daha uzun dalga boylarına doğru azalmıştır.

**İleriye Bakış**
Yazarlara göre bu çalışma, kısa zaman ölçekli yıldız değişkenliğine yeni bir gözlemsel pencere açıyor. Ayrıca geçiş yapan gezegenleri incelemek için kullanılan ışık eğrilerindeki renge bağlı yıldız gürültüsünü karakterize etmenin bir yolunu sunuyor.

papers.title: Companions of Hot Jupiters: two decades of radial velocity monitoring with CORALIE
papers.abstract: Hot Jupiters are thought to form through multiple pathways, some of which can leave observable signatures in the architecture of their planetary systems. Massive outer companions, in particular, can provide important constraints on the dynamical histories of hot Jupiters. We aim to characterize the occurrence rate and orbital properties of additional giant companions in hot Jupiter systems, and to investigate whether these companions provide evidence for the role of dynamical interactions in shaping the hot Jupiter population. We perform a homogeneous long-term radial-velocity analysis of 147 WASP hot Jupiter systems observed with the CORALIE spectrograph between 2007 and 2025. We identify or refine 13 outer giant companions and use individual radial-velocity posteriors within a Bayesian occurrence-rate framework to measure the frequency of giant companions over orbital periods of 10--6250 days. The occurrence rate of additional giant companions increases strongly with orbital period, from 2lt;0.01$ and 0.02 at 10--50 and 50--250 days to 0.05 and 0.17 at 250--1250 and 1250--6250 days, respectively, in agreement with the giant-planet occurrence of the general FGK population and with previous estimates of outer companions to hot Jupiters. Hot Jupiters with detected companions have longer orbital periods and higher eccentricities than those without. We also find that companion eccentricity decreases with hot Jupiter period, and that the companion-to-hot-Jupiter mass ratio increases with period ratio, both consistent with expectations from high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Our results support HEM as the mechanism shaping hot Jupiters with outer companions. Combining long-baseline radial velocities with future Gaia astrometry will further constrain companion masses, mutual inclinations, and dynamical histories.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Hot Jupiters are giant planets that circle their stars in just a few days, far closer than Mercury orbits our Sun. They almost certainly did not form there, so astronomers want to know how they got so close. One theory says a distant companion gave the planet a gravitational shove, sending it onto a stretched-out path that was later pulled into a tight circle. If so, the hot Jupiter's neighbors should carry clues about this violent past.

**What They Did**
The team studied 147 hot Jupiter systems found by the WASP survey (Wide Angle Search for Planets). They used nearly two decades of data, from 2007 to 2025, from the CORALIE spectrograph. This instrument measures how a star wobbles toward and away from us as unseen planets tug on it, a technique called radial velocity. Because all the systems were analyzed the same way, the results can be compared fairly. The team found or refined 13 outer giant companions. They then used a statistical method to work out how common such companions are at different orbital periods, from 10 to 6,250 days.

**Key Findings**
Companions are rare close in and more common far out. Fewer than 1 in 100 systems have a giant companion with an orbit of 10–50 days, and about 2 in 100 for 50–250 days. The rate rises to about 5 in 100 for 250–1,250 days and 17 in 100 for 1,250–6,250 days. This matches how common giant planets are around ordinary Sun-like stars. Hot Jupiters with companions tend to have longer orbital periods and more stretched-out orbits. Companion orbits are less eccentric when the hot Jupiter's period is longer, and the companion's mass compared with the hot Jupiter's grows as the gap between their orbits widens. The authors say these patterns fit high-eccentricity migration, the shove-then-settle story.

**Looking Forward**
Radial velocity cannot reveal everything about a companion, such as how tilted its orbit is. Future data from the Gaia space telescope, which tracks the tiny sideways motions of stars, combined with these long records should pin down companion masses and orbital alignments, and reveal more about how hot Jupiters formed.

The team studied 147 hot Jupiter systems found by the WASP survey (Wide Angle Search for Planets). They used nearly two decades of data, from 2007 to 2025, from the CORALIE spectrograph. This instrument measures how a star wobbles toward and away from us as unseen planets tug on it, a technique called radial velocity. Because all the systems were analyzed the same way, the results can be compared fairly. The team found or refined 13 outer giant companions. They then used a statistical method to work out how common such companions are at different orbital periods, from 10 to 6,250 days.

Key Findings

Companions are rare close in and more common far out. Fewer than 1 in 100 systems have a giant companion with an orbit of 10–50 days, and about 2 in 100 for 50–250 days. The rate rises to about 5 in 100 for 250–1,250 days and 17 in 100 for 1,250–6,250 days. This matches how common giant planets are around ordinary Sun-like stars. Hot Jupiters with companions tend to have longer orbital periods and more stretched-out orbits. Companion orbits are less eccentric when the hot Jupiter's period is longer, and the companion's mass compared with the hot Jupiter's grows as the gap between their orbits widens. The authors say these patterns fit high-eccentricity migration, the shove-then-settle story.

Looking Forward

Radial velocity cannot reveal everything about a companion, such as how tilted its orbit is. Future data from the Gaia space telescope, which tracks the tiny sideways motions of stars, combined with these long records should pin down companion masses and orbital alignments, and reveal more about how hot Jupiters formed.

papers.title_tr: Sıcak Jüpiterlerin Yoldaşları: CORALIE ile yirmi yıllık radyal hız izlemesi

Tüm sistemler aynı yöntemle çözümlendiği için sonuçlar adil biçimde karşılaştırılabiliyor. Ekip, 13 dış dev yoldaşı buldu ya da bunların özelliklerini iyileştirdi. Yoldaşlar yıldıza yakın bölgelerde nadir, uzak bölgelerde ise daha yaygındır. 10–50 günlük yörüngelerde dev yoldaş bulunma oranı yüzde 1'in altındadır, 50–250 günde ise yaklaşık yüzde 2'dir. Yoldaşı olan sıcak Jüpiterlerin yörünge periyotları daha uzundur ve yörüngeleri daha basıktır. papers.title: Robustness of C/O and mean molecular weight under disequilibrium chemistry
papers.abstract: Transmission spectroscopy increasingly reduces exoplanet spectra to derived compositional metrics, such as C/O, O/H, and mean molecular weight (MMW), but these quantities do not carry molecular abundance uncertainties in the same way. We assessed the reliability of these metrics for hot Jupiters and sub-Neptunes, by combining analytic uncertainty propagation with photochemical VULCAN forward models and representative published retrieval constraints. Propagating molecular abundance uncertainties produced substantially larger fractional uncertainties in elemental abundance ratios than in MMW. The fractional uncertainties in C/O and O/H were typically comparable to the inferred ratios, whereas the fractional uncertainty in MMW was more than two orders of magnitude smaller in H2/He-dominated atmospheres. Photochemistry and vertical mixing redistributed individual molecules but produced only minor changes in C/O and MMW at the pressures probed by transmission spectroscopy. C/O remains an important diagnostic of atmospheric chemistry and planetary formation history, but its interpretation requires careful uncertainty propagation. Mean molecular weight may provide a comparatively stable population-level diagnostic for linking observable atmospheres to bulk composition, especially across the sub-Neptune radius valley.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
When telescopes study the atmospheres of planets beyond our solar system, scientists often boil a complex light pattern down to a few headline numbers. These include the carbon-to-oxygen ratio (C/O), the oxygen-to-hydrogen ratio (O/H), and the mean molecular weight (MMW), which is the average "heaviness" of the gas particles in an atmosphere. Researchers use these numbers to infer how planets formed. But a headline number is only as trustworthy as the measurements behind it.

**What They Did**
The team studied two kinds of worlds: hot Jupiters, giant gas planets orbiting very close to their stars, and sub-Neptunes, planets between Earth and Neptune in size. They worked out mathematically how uncertainty in the measured amounts of individual molecules carries through into each headline number. They also ran VULCAN, a computer model that simulates how starlight-driven chemistry and vertical mixing of gas reshuffle molecules. They compared the results with uncertainty levels from published analyses of real observations.

**Key Findings**
Uncertainties grew much larger for the element ratios than for MMW. The fractional uncertainties in C/O and O/H were typically about as large as the ratios themselves. That is like measuring a table as "one metre, give or take one metre." In atmospheres dominated by hydrogen and helium, the fractional uncertainty in MMW was more than two orders of magnitude smaller, meaning over a hundred times smaller. Photochemistry and mixing moved individual molecules around, but they changed C/O and MMW only slightly at the depths probed by transmission spectroscopy. This technique studies starlight filtering through a planet's atmosphere.

**Looking Forward**
C/O remains a valuable clue to atmospheric chemistry and planet formation, but it must be handled with careful accounting of uncertainty. MMW may be a steadier measure. It could offer a dependable way to connect observable atmospheres to a planet's overall makeup across whole populations of planets. This is especially promising for sub-Neptunes on either side of the "radius valley," a dip in how common planets of certain sizes are.

papers.title_tr: Dengesizlik kimyası altında C/O ve ortalama molekül ağırlığının sağlamlığı
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Teleskoplar güneş sistemimizin dışındaki gezegenlerin atmosferlerini incelerken, bilim insanları karmaşık bir ışık desenini çoğu zaman birkaç temel sayıya indirger. Bunlar karbon-oksijen oranı (C/O), oksijen-hidrojen oranı (O/H) ve ortalama molekül ağırlığıdır (MMW). Ortalama molekül ağırlığı, bir atmosferdeki gaz parçacıklarının ortalama "ağırlığı" demektir. Araştırmacılar bu sayıları gezegenlerin nasıl oluştuğunu çıkarsamak için kullanır. Ancak bir sayı, arkasındaki ölçümler kadar güvenilirdir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip iki tür dünyayı inceledi: yıldızlarına çok yakın yörüngede dönen devasa gaz gezegenler olan sıcak Jüpiterler ve boyut olarak Dünya ile Neptün arasında kalan alt-Neptünler. Önce tek tek moleküllerin ölçülen miktarlarındaki belirsizliğin her bir temel sayıya nasıl yansıdığını matematiksel olarak hesapladılar. Ardından, yıldız ışığının tetiklediği kimyanın ve gazın dikey karışımının molekülleri nasıl yeniden dağıttığını simüle eden VULCAN adlı bir bilgisayar modelini çalıştırdılar. Sonuçları, gerçek gözlemlerin yayımlanmış analizlerindeki belirsizlik düzeyleriyle karşılaştırdılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Belirsizlikler, element oranlarında MMW'ye kıyasla çok daha fazla büyüdü. C/O ve O/H'nin bağıl belirsizlikleri genellikle oranların kendisi kadar büyüktü. Bu, bir masayı "bir metre, artı eksi bir metre" diye ölçmeye benzer. Hidrojen ve helyumun baskın olduğu atmosferlerde MMW'nin bağıl belirsizliği ise iki büyüklük mertebesinden fazla, yani yüz kattan fazla daha küçüktü. Fotokimya ve karışım tek tek molekülleri yer değiştirdi, ancak geçiş tayfölçümünün (yıldız ışığının gezegenin atmosferinden süzülerek geçmesini inceleyen yöntem) sınadığı basınç düzeylerinde C/O ve MMW'yi yalnızca az miktarda değiştirdi.

**İleriye Bakış**
C/O, atmosfer kimyası ve gezegen oluşumu için hâlâ değerli bir ipucudur, ancak belirsizliklerin dikkatle hesaba katılmasını gerektirir. MMW ise daha kararlı bir ölçü olabilir. Gözlenebilen atmosferleri bir gezegenin genel yapısına bağlamak için, gezegen topluluğu düzeyinde güvenilir bir yol sunabilir. Bu, özellikle "yarıçap vadisi"nin (belirli boyutlardaki gezegenlerin görülme sıklığındaki bir düşüş) iki yanındaki alt-Neptünler için umut vericidir.

papers.title: Single-Transit Parameter Estimation with Calibrated Uncertainties
papers.abstract: The growing volume of photometric data from current and upcoming exoplanet surveys demands automated analysis pipelines to detect and characterize exoplanet transit signals. Among these, single-transit events present a challenge, since only one event is observed, and standard transit-fitting techniques for periodic signals do not directly apply because they rely on phase-folding. Beyond detection, characterizing these events is equally critical for follow-up, yet existing approaches are either sensitive to stellar variability and require prior detrending, or depend on stellar priors and per-target fitting. This work presents a convolutional neural network that predicts transit depth, duration, and mid-transit time, together with calibrated uncertainties, directly from a single transit signal. Our network is trained on synthetic light curves and evaluated against a trapezoidal least-squares baseline. On 120 confirmed exoplanets, both methods achieve comparable median errors, but the baseline fails to locate the transit in 10% of cases, producing unreliable estimates that would propagate into follow-up prioritization. In contrast, our network fails in only 1% of cases, yields lower mean absolute errors, and does not require detrending or stellar priors. Detrending would distort or remove the transit along with high stellar variability, precisely where the baseline fails and our network succeeds. Finally, we identify 169 new transit candidates in TESS Sectors 27-60 and apply our approach to obtain their physical parameters, creating a catalog that includes single-transit, multi-transit and multi-planet systems. This approach offers a scalable path toward automated characterization of single transit events, a population that will grow with upcoming surveys.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Imagine watching a distant streetlight for months and catching a single moment when something passes in front of it. That is the problem astronomers face with "single transits": a planet crosses in front of its star only once during the observations, dimming the starlight briefly. Telescopes such as TESS (the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) collect huge amounts of data, and upcoming surveys will find even more of these one-time events. The usual methods for measuring a planet's signal depend on seeing the dip repeat and stacking the repeats together, so they don't work here. Other approaches need the star's brightness "cleaned up" first, or need prior knowledge of the star. That cleaning can distort or erase the very dip being studied.

**What They Did**
The researchers built a convolutional neural network, a type of artificial intelligence that is good at recognizing patterns. They trained it on synthetic (computer-made) light curves, which are records of a star's brightness over time. From one transit, the network estimates three things: how deep the dip is, how long it lasts, and when its midpoint occurs. It also gives calibrated uncertainties, meaning error bars that honestly reflect how much to trust each answer. They compared it with a standard method called trapezoidal least-squares fitting, which models the dip as a trapezoid.

**Key Findings**
On 120 confirmed exoplanets, both methods had comparable median errors. The baseline method failed to find the transit in 10% of cases, while the network failed in only 1%. The network also had lower mean absolute errors and needed no detrending or stellar priors. It worked well on stars with strong brightness variability, where cleaning the data would damage the signal. The team also identified 169 new transit candidates in TESS Sectors 27–60 and estimated their physical parameters. The resulting catalog includes single-transit, multi-transit and multi-planet systems.

**Looking Forward**
As surveys grow, single-transit events will become more common, and astronomers will need fast, automated ways to decide which ones deserve follow-up observations. This approach offers a scalable route to doing that, with trustworthy error bars to help prioritize targets.

papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Uzaktaki bir sokak lambasını aylarca izlediğinizi ve yalnızca bir kez önünden bir şeyin geçtiğini gördüğünüzü düşünün. Ayrıca kalibre edilmiş belirsizlikler, yani her cevaba ne kadar güvenilebileceğini dürüstçe yansıtan hata payları da veriyor. Sonuçları, ışık azalmasını yamuk biçiminde modelleyen yamuk en küçük kareler uydurması adlı standart bir yöntemle karşılaştırdılar.

Sektörlerinde 169 yeni geçiş adayı belirledi ve bunların fiziksel parametrelerini kestirdi. Ortaya çıkan katalog; tek geçişli, çok geçişli ve çok gezegenli sistemleri içeriyor.

Taramalar büyüdükçe tek geçiş olayları daha yaygın hâle gelecek ve gökbilimcilerin hangilerinin takip gözlemlerine değer olduğuna karar vermek için hızlı, otomatik yöntemlere ihtiyacı olacak. papers.title: A 36.34-day Sub-Neptune Candidate Transiting the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 402710280
papers.abstract: We report a transiting sub-Neptune candidate with a period of 36.34 days around TIC 402710280 (TYC 9041-03677-1), a K dwarf of TESS magnitude 9.24 at 66.8 pc that the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) has observed only in full-frame images. Four transits, recorded between 2021 and 2026 in Sectors 39, 93, 100 and 102 and reduced by three independent pipelines, share a depth of 2092 ± 47 ppm and a duration of 5.27 ± 0.05 h. Two of them fall on consecutive cycles, and every shorter period predicts transits in covered data that are absent at ≥ 18.6σ; the period is P = 36.33986 ± 0.00051 d. A transit model gives Rₚ/R_ = 0.0421⁺⁰.⁰⁰⁰⁷₋₀.₀₀₀₅ and a stellar density consistent with the host's. The candidate has a radius of 3.75 ± 0.22 R_⊕ and an equilibrium temperature of 498 ± 21 K. Difference-image centroids place the signal 1.5'' ± 1.3'' from the target. The only catalogued star close enough to contribute, a background star 3.5'' away, would have to host an eclipsing binary whose eclipse shape is disfavoured for any main-sequence pair (Δχ² ≥ 142). No secondary eclipse is detected, and TRICERATOPS gives a false-positive probability of 0.003 ± 0.004. No high-resolution imaging exists, so companions within about 1'' are constrained only by Gaia astrometry. The mid-times scatter about a linear ephemeris by 21.8 min (rms). Quick-Look Pipeline light curves reproduce the 29-min excess in the interval between the two 2026 transits, so it does not arise in our photometry; we report the scatter without choosing between an instrumental and a dynamical origin. The light curve also contains a 407 ± 26 ppm signal with a period of 3.78 days whose source, the target or the background star, the present data cannot identify. We predict transit times, including one in TESS Sector 114 on 2027 February 19.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
Planets larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune are among the most common in the galaxy, yet our own solar system has none. Learning what they are made of means finding them around bright, nearby stars, where follow-up observations are easiest. This new candidate circles TIC 402710280, an orange K dwarf (a star somewhat cooler and smaller than the Sun) about 218 light-years away. It is a candidate, not a confirmed planet.

**What They Did**
NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) has only seen this star in "full-frame images," wide snapshots of the sky rather than dedicated pointings. In those snapshots the team found four small dips in starlight, called transits, recorded between 2021 and 2026. Three independent software pipelines processed the data. Two dips fell on back-to-back orbits, and the team showed that any shorter orbital period would predict dips in covered data that are not there. They then hunted for impostors. They checked where on the sky the dimming comes from, whether a faint background star 3.5 arcseconds away could be hiding a pair of eclipsing stars, and whether a secondary eclipse appears. They also ran a statistical tool called TRICERATOPS.

**Key Findings**
The candidate orbits every 36.34 days. Each transit dims the star by about 0.2% and lasts roughly 5.3 hours. That implies a planet about 3.75 times Earth's radius with an equilibrium temperature near 498 kelvin (about 225 °C). The dimming sits within 1.5 ± 1.3 arcseconds of the target. The background-star scenario requires eclipse shapes that are disfavoured for ordinary stars. No secondary eclipse was seen, and the false-positive probability is 0.003 ± 0.004. There are caveats. No high-resolution imaging exists, so very close companions are constrained only by Gaia astrometry. The transit times wander by about 21.8 minutes from a perfectly regular clock. The authors do not decide whether that comes from instruments or from gravitational tugs by another body. A separate 3.78-day signal also appears, and its source is unknown.

**Looking Forward**
The team predicts future transit times, including one in TESS Sector 114 on 19 February 2027. Those observations, plus high-resolution imaging, could test the timing wobble and strengthen the planetary interpretation.

papers.title_tr: Yakındaki K Cücesi TIC 402710280'i Geçen 36,34 Günlük Bir Alt-Neptün Adayı
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
Dünya'dan büyük ama Neptün'den küçük gezegenler galaksideki en yaygın gezegenler arasındadır, ancak kendi Güneş Sistemimizde böyle bir gezegen yoktur. Bu gezegenlerin neden yapıldığını anlamak için, takip gözlemlerinin en kolay olduğu parlak ve yakın yıldızların çevresinde bulunmaları gerekir. Bu yeni aday, yaklaşık 218 ışık yılı uzaklıktaki turuncu bir K cücesi (Güneş'ten biraz daha soğuk ve küçük bir yıldız) olan TIC 402710280'in etrafında dönüyor. Yine de bu bir adaydır, doğrulanmış bir gezegen değildir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
NASA'nın Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) uydusu bu yıldızı yalnızca "tam çerçeve görüntülerinde" gördü. Bunlar tek bir yıldıza odaklanmak yerine gökyüzünün geniş bir bölgesini kaydeden görüntülerdir. Ekip bu görüntülerde, 2021 ile 2026 arasında kaydedilmiş, geçiş adı verilen dört küçük ışık azalması buldu. Veriler üç bağımsız yazılım hattıyla işlendi. İki geçiş art arda gelen yörünge turlarında gerçekleşti. Ekip, daha kısa herhangi bir yörünge döneminin, veri bulunan zamanlarda gözlenmeyen geçişleri öngöreceğini gösterdi. Ardından taklitçileri araştırdılar. Sönmenin gökyüzünde nereden geldiğini, 3,5 yay saniyesi uzaktaki sönük bir arka plan yıldızının tutulmalı bir çift yıldızı barındırıp barındıramayacağını ve ikincil tutulma olup olmadığını incelediler. Ayrıca TRICERATOPS adlı istatistiksel bir araç kullandılar.

**Ana Bulgular**
Aday her 36,34 günde bir yörüngesini tamamlıyor. Her geçiş yıldızın ışığını yaklaşık %0,2 azaltıyor ve kabaca 5,3 saat sürüyor. Bu, yarıçapı Dünya'nın yaklaşık 3,75 katı ve denge sıcaklığı yaklaşık 498 kelvin (yaklaşık 225 °C) olan bir gezegene işaret ediyor. Sönme, hedefin 1,5 ± 1,3 yay saniyesi içinde yer alıyor. Arka plan yıldızı senaryosu, sıradan yıldızlar için olası görülmeyen tutulma biçimleri gerektiriyor. İkincil tutulma saptanmadı ve yanlış pozitif olasılığı 0,003 ± 0,004. Bazı çekinceler var. Yüksek çözünürlüklü görüntü bulunmadığından çok yakın eşlikçiler yalnızca Gaia astrometrisiyle sınırlanabiliyor. Geçiş zamanları düzenli bir saatten yaklaşık 21,8 dakika sapıyor. Yazarlar bunun aletlerden mi yoksa başka bir cismin kütleçekimsel etkisinden mi kaynaklandığına karar vermiyor. Ayrıca kaynağı bilinmeyen, 3,78 günlük ayrı bir sinyal de var.

**İleriye Bakış**
Ekip, TESS'in 114. Gözlem Diliminde 19 Şubat 2027'de beklenen bir geçiş de dahil olmak üzere gelecekteki geçiş zamanlarını öngörüyor. Bu gözlemler ve yüksek çözünürlüklü görüntüleme, zamanlama sapmasını sınayabilir ve gezegen yorumunu güçlendirebilir.

papers.title: Kinematic structure and age of a Scorpius--Centaurus subcomponent: implications for PDS 70 planetary system
papers.abstract: PDS 70, the only system with two directly imaged protoplanets embedded in their natal disk, is a benchmark for giant-planet formation theory. Interpreting the planetary luminosities requires a precise age for the host star, but the widely adopted isochronal age of 5.4±1.0 Myr is substantially younger than ages inferred for the Upper Centaurus--Lupus (UCL) population with which it is associated. We address this discrepancy by determining a new kinematic age for PDS 70 using radial velocities for 405 candidate members of the Scorpius--Centaurus T subcomponent from the Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) on the ANU 2.3 m telescope, reducing uncertainties by a factor of 5.5 compared to Gaia. %We supplement these measurements with Hα and lithium equivalent widths as youth diagnostics. We combine these with Gaia DR3 astrometry in the Chronostar kinematic reconstruction framework to derive a posterior-weighted kinematic age of approximately 10--15 Myr for all the T subcomponent stars, with a kinematic age of ≈ 12--16 Myr for PDS 70, ruling out ages as young as the published isochronal estimate. At this kinematic age, PDS 70 b's (and to a lesser extent, PDS 70 c's) luminosity is incompatible with warm-start cooling tracks under current dynamical mass constraints. The most natural interpretation is that PDS 70 b formed ≈10.5 Myr after its host star, and no less than ≈7.7 Myr after it.
papers.summary:
**Why It Matters**
PDS 70 is a young star circled by two baby planets that astronomers have photographed directly while they are still growing inside the disk of gas and dust that made them. That makes it a benchmark for how giant planets form. But a planet's brightness only reveals its story if we know its age, much as a candle's remaining length means little unless you know when it was lit. The star's commonly used age of 5.4 million years (give or take 1 million) is much younger than the ages found for the larger stellar group it belongs to, Upper Centaurus–Lupus.

**What They Did**
Instead of judging the star's age by its brightness and color, the team traced how stars move. Stars born together drift apart over time, so running their motions backward shows when they were last bunched together. The team used the Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) on the Australian National University 2.3-metre telescope to measure how fast 405 candidate members of a Scorpius–Centaurus subgroup, called the T subcomponent, move toward or away from us. These measurements were 5.5 times more precise than those from the Gaia space telescope. They combined them with Gaia's sky positions and motions in a modelling framework called Chronostar.

**Key Findings**
The T subcomponent stars have a kinematic age of roughly 10–15 million years, and PDS 70 itself comes out at about 12–16 million years. That rules out ages as young as the published 5.4 million. At this older age, the brightness of planet PDS 70 b, and to a lesser degree planet c, does not match the "warm-start" cooling models, which assume a planet begins hot and fades, given current estimates of its mass. The most natural explanation is that planet b formed about 10.5 million years after its star, and no less than about 7.7 million years after it.

**Looking Forward**
If this holds, giant planets may be able to form much later in a disk's life than many theories assume. Better mass measurements and further tests of the age will show whether the planets really are late arrivals.

papers.title_tr: Scorpius–Centaurus alt bileşeninin kinematik yapısı ve yaşı: PDS 70 gezegen sistemi için çıkarımlar
papers.summary_tr:
**Neden Önemli**
PDS 70, etrafında iki bebek gezegen dönen genç bir yıldızdır. Bu gezegenler, kendilerini oluşturan gaz ve toz diskinin içinde hâlâ büyürken doğrudan görüntülenmiştir. Bu nedenle sistem, dev gezegenlerin nasıl oluştuğunu anlamak için bir ölçüt niteliğindedir. Ancak bir gezegenin parlaklığı, yaşı bilinmedikçe pek bir şey anlatmaz; tıpkı bir mumun kalan boyunun, ne zaman yakıldığını bilmeden anlam taşımaması gibi. Yıldız için yaygın olarak kullanılan 5,4 milyon yıllık yaş (artı eksi 1 milyon yıl), ait olduğu daha büyük yıldız topluluğu Upper Centaurus–Lupus için bulunan yaşlardan çok daha gençtir.

**Ne Yaptılar**
Ekip, yıldızın yaşını parlaklığına ve rengine bakarak tahmin etmek yerine yıldızların hareketini izledi. Birlikte doğan yıldızlar zamanla birbirinden uzaklaşır. Hareketleri geriye doğru sarıldığında, yıldızların en son ne zaman bir arada olduğu görülebilir. Araştırmacılar, Avustralya Ulusal Üniversitesi'nin 2,3 metrelik teleskobundaki Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) ile Scorpius–Centaurus'un T alt bileşeni denen kümesinin 405 aday üyesinin bize doğru ya da bizden uzağa hızını ölçtü. Bu ölçümler Gaia uzay teleskobununkilerden 5,5 kat daha hassastı. Ekip bunları, Gaia'nın gökyüzü konumları ve hareketleriyle birlikte Chronostar adlı modelleme çerçevesinde kullandı.

**Ana Bulgular**
T alt bileşeni yıldızlarının kinematik yaşı yaklaşık 10–15 milyon yıl çıktı. PDS 70'in kendisi için ise yaklaşık 12–16 milyon yıl bulundu. Bu sonuç, yayımlanmış 5,4 milyon yıl kadar genç yaşları dışarıda bırakıyor. Bu daha ileri yaşta, PDS 70 b gezegeninin ve daha az ölçüde c gezegeninin parlaklığı, mevcut kütle tahminleri göz önüne alındığında "sıcak başlangıç" soğuma modelleriyle uyuşmuyor. En doğal açıklama, b gezegeninin yıldızından yaklaşık 10,5 milyon yıl sonra ve en az yaklaşık 7,7 milyon yıl sonra oluşmuş olmasıdır.

**İleriye Bakış**
Bu sonuç doğruysa, dev gezegenler bir diskin ömrünün birçok kuramın varsaydığından çok daha geç bir döneminde de oluşabilir. Daha iyi kütle ölçümleri ve yaşın yeni testleri, bu gezegenlerin gerçekten geç geldiğini gösterecektir.
